notes: The programme's own page says the language is Dutch, so Dutch language proficiency (B2) applies to foreign-diploma applicants per the general Inholland entry-requirements pages. The Business Studies page itself does not mention a language test, but the institution's rules for buitenlands diploma require it. The instellingscollegegeld (€ 10,360 for 2026-2027) is the institution-wide rate for students who do not qualify for the statutory fee; a non-EU student pays this rate. The documents listed come from the general In- en uitschrijfregels and may not be the complete visa/MVV list (see the Suriname visa page for that country-specific list).

evidence.quote: Students who have completed their prior education abroad must therefore demonstrate Dutch language proficiency at B2 level (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages).
This can be done by obtaining an NT2 (Dutch as a Second Language) Programme II certificate (reading, writing, speaking and listening components).
